newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice exporters worried over EU export delay.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice exporters worried over EU export delay.

text.p: Thai rice exporters are worried that the European Union's slow approval process for importers' licenses will affect Thai rice exports under duty-free and low-tariff programs to the EU, trade sources said on Monday.
They also complained about uncertainty over the delivery period for rice exports, the sources said.
Exporters complained of lengthy delays in issuing licenses for EU importers. EU importers have to submit details of Thai export licenses to support their requests for import quotas, the sources said.

Thailand has received quotas to export 21,455 tonnes of white rice without any tariff to the EU for 1996. It could also export 1,812 tonnes of cargo rice at the tariff rate of 88 ecus a tonne below current duty rate and 31,200 tonnes of broken rice with tariff reduction of 28 ecus per tonnes.

Moreover, it was not clear whether the EU counted December 31 as a deadline for shipment or arrival date in Europe. They also did not know whether an import license for any EU country would cover re-export for another destination within the group.
"The commerce ministry seemed to be confused about this as well. Exporters had asked officials to check and spell it out for them," one trader said.
